subject: Private deployment qualification: VPC networking, KMS, and IP rotation
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@fintrust.com>, FinTrust NetOps <netops@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment qualification: VPC networking, KMS, and IP rotation

Hi Samir / NetOps team —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can prepare the next NetOps deep-dive: 

Summary from call:
- FinTrust wants to evaluate Private VPC (customer VPC + PrivateLink) for production inference.
- Primary non-negotiables: customer-managed KMS for model request encryption, and an IP allowlist for egress to Redwood endpoints.
- You indicated internal policy requires public egress IP rotation every 7 days and a central NAT/egress owner.

Action items / questions for NetOps
1) KMS: confirm whether you can provide a customer-managed KMS ARN (AWS KMS or equivalent) and any key policy constraints we should be aware of. Please attach an example ARN if available.
2) Egress / IP rotation: you mentioned weekly rotation — can you confirm an acceptable CIDR range or a mechanism (e.g., AWS NAT gateway + Elastic IP pool) for stable allowlisting during rotation windows?
3) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering: any constraints that would preclude PrivateLink (private endpoint) for our connector? In particular, does your security policy allow incoming PrivateLink endpoints into your subnet architecture?
4) Ownership: who will own firewall/NAT/egress config and change window approvals on your side (role & email)?
5) Evidence: FinTrust security requested SOC2 plus network flow logs for onboarding. Who should we send the evidence checklist to?

Attachments: call-transcript-stub.txt, draft-redwood-privatedeploy-connector.pdf (see referenced sections for required firewall ports).

Proposed next step: schedule a 45-min NetOps deep-dive (technical) this week. Please suggest 2 times.

Thanks,
Olga
--
Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@fintrust.com>

Cc: FinTrust NetOps <netops@fintrust.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment qualification: VPC networking, KMS, and IP rotation

Olga — thanks for the thorough recap. Couple of clarifications from NetOps: 

1) KMS: We prefer customer-managed AWS KMS. I'll circulate a sample ARN in a follow-up (can't paste the live ARN here). Key policy: NetOps requires a cross-account grant to Redwood's service principal; we can provide that during the workshop.
2) IP rotation: we rotate outbound EIPs on our NATs on a 7-day cadence. For allowlisting, we can provide a 3-day overlap window where old+new EIPs are valid to reduce disruption. We'll need Redwood to support quickly updating your allowlist via API or have a pre-approved set of /28s.
3) PrivateLink: Our infra team prefers PrivateLink for isolation, but a few of our application subnets sit in a restricted zone that blocks endpoint creation. We'll need to validate which subnets can accept endpoints.
4) Ownership: NetOps (netops@fintrust.com) will own the NAT and firewall config. App infra (app-ops@fintrust.com) will own service-side endpoint requests.
5) Evidence: security@fintrust.com expects a short mapping of SOC2 controls + where flow logs will be stored (S3 bucket or Splunk).

Attaching the initial network diagram we sketched during the call.

Samir
--
Samir Khan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, FinTrust
samir.k@fintrust.com
[Attachment: fintrust-netops-initial-diagram.pdf (application/pdf)]

Looping back with a few technical clarifications for the packet and the deep-dive agenda: 

- PrivateLink vs Peering: Redwood supports both. PrivateLink is preferred for tenancy isolation and avoids cross-VPC routing complexity; however, if FinTrust blocks endpoint creation in some subnets, peering + route limits may be required. We'll ask NetOps to confirm which subnets can accept endpoints ahead of the call.
- Egress ports: typical ports we need open: 443 outbound to Redwood connector endpoints; optional 1491 for metrics ingestion (if NetOps wants agent-based telemetry). We'll include a minimal ports list in the packet.
- IP ranges: If NetOps can provide a rolling list of Elastic IPs in /28 blocks (or at least a signed list daily), Redwood can support an API-driven allowlist update. Our platform can accept programmatic updates with a 5-minute propagation SLA for hosted firewall rules.
- KMS flow: customer-managed KMS with a cross-account grant works. We need an IAM role ARN for Redwood to assume for envelope encryption operations; we'll document the least-privileged policy in the packet.

Attachment: privatelink-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

I'll draft the technical slide for the deep-dive and drop it in the HubSpot record. If NetOps can confirm times, let's lock in Wed 07/25 09:00 PT.

Thanks,
Karthik
